whatTheyArgued: Purva Mimamsa Sutra 1.1.2 (Jha 1916, verbatim snip): dharma or duty is the desirable thing indicated by Vedic injunction (codana). Jha's commentary frames the point as an epistemic one: there is a valid means of knowing dharma, namely the Vedic injunction, since it lies beyond senses and inference. A nearby sutra (1.2.19) argues a vidhi (injunction) is an injunction because it lays down something new (apurva) that is not otherwise known. I found no statement in what I read that an injunction 'persists until discharged', nor that discharge is a recorded act.

scholarship.ref: Wikipedia 'Purva Mimamsa Sutras' (fetched; weak, used for dating and structure only)
scholarship.supports: text c. 300-200 BCE in twelve chapters; 1.1.2 'duty is that which is indicated by Vedic injunctions'; Sabara's commentary is the main complete one
scholarship.disputes: Not a scholarly source. No SEP/IEP page could be fetched (404s), so no peer-reviewed treatment of obligation, apurva or nitya-karma persistence was read. The notion of an unfulfilled duty continuing (as in later nitya karma and apurva doctrine) I know only in general and did not verify.

ourUse: obligations.js: an injunction opens a standing obligation record (id, grounds, consequences, persistence counter); carryObligations increments persistence on each carry unless status is resolved/closed/superseded; resolveObligation records the discharge as an operation. Header: 'after Mimamsa's vidhi: a scriptural injunction opens a standing obligation that persists until the enjoined act discharges it.'

bends.ours: Compendium: 'An injunction persists until it is discharged; it does not fade with neglect, and discharging it is a recorded act, not an assumption.' Credit given to Jaimini.
bends.theirs: The verified sutra defines dharma by its source of knowledge (injunction). Persistence, neglect and recorded discharge are not in the passage read; they are our design (or later Mimamsa doctrine, unverified by me).

bends.ours: Any declared grounds may open an obligation (pledges, promises, tasks); topics include 'pledge'.
bends.theirs: Mimamsa duty is what Vedic injunction teaches; the sutra argues it cannot be known from perception or inference, which excludes our everyday use.

bends.ours: The injunction creates a ledger entry that stays open.
bends.theirs: The sutra concerns how dharma is known (injunction as the only means), not an object's lifetime.
